svg.title: fig06
svg.desc: Figure 6 | Behavioural trade-offs between DANCeRS and ORCA. Paired native-model DANCeRS-minus-ORCA contrasts across 20 open missions for (a) all-agent completion time, (b) mean path length, (c) mean velocity total variation, (d) mean acceleration RMS, (e) mean jerk RMS, and (f) minimum pair clearance. Squares show registered estimates; whiskers show 95% intervals; the dashed line indicates zero difference. Every panel retains its own metric unit and horizontal scale. Both methods complete all agents in these open missions. DANCeRS has longer paths and later completion, lower acceleration and jerk RMS, and higher velocity variation. The clearance interval crosses zero. All 12 registered behavioural metrics and the three paired DANCeRS implementation-resource ratios are retained in data.csv; six nonredundant behavioural metrics are plotted. Results depend on the fixed inputs, registered parameter mapping, native motion models, and host. Circle tasks and cadence sensitivity belong to Extended Data.
